business_problem: Trend Micro needed to bring its domain-specific Cybertron cybersecurity LLM into production quickly while preserving self-hosting, data sovereignty, auditability, and secure inference controls for enterprise and government environments.
solution_summary: Trend Micro uses NVIDIA Universal LLM NIM Microservice technology to package and run its proprietary Trend Cybertron cybersecurity LLM on NVIDIA Enterprise AI factories across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments. Cybertron is described as a security-specific model trained on years of risk intelligence, telemetry, adversarial tactics, MITRE ATT&CK techniques, SIEM logs, natural-language risk reports, and red-team narratives. Universal NIM lets Trend deploy these custom models without waiting for engine-level optimization, while keeping deployment flexible across supported backends and allowing the company to self-host sensitive workloads. The page emphasizes zero-trust inference, sovereign AI readiness, and controlled handling of training data, intellectual property, and customer telemetry. Trend also describes monitoring inference behavior in production and using NVIDIA NeMo Data Flywheel for retraining loops over time. For agentic security scenarios, the architecture can connect Cybertron with AI-Q Blueprint patterns so AI agents can reason over security knowledge bases, telemetry logs, and threat intelligence in real time.
